paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the LORD wins, and He doesn't just win the fight, He wins the whole world. The passage opens with nations gathered against Jerusalem and a city in a rough spot, but it ends with the LORD as King. Zechariah says, "On that day the LORD will become King over all the earth—the LORD alone, and His name alone." (Zechariah 14:9) Every hard moment in this prophecy is leading to that line.

Now look at who ends up worshiping. Survivors from the very nations that came against Jerusalem go up "year after year to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts." (Zechariah 14:16) I did NOT see that coming, and I've been surprised by a lot of ovens. The prophecy also says Jerusalem will "dwell securely" (Zechariah 14:11), so the people of God can hold on to hope even when things look rough.

Then the prophecy gets close to home. "HOLY TO THE LORD" will be on the horses' bells, and every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be "holy to the LORD of Hosts." (Zechariah 14:20-21) So even the everyday stuff gets set apart for Him. I think that's an invitation, baker: under the King, nothing in your day is too small or too ordinary to belong to Him. And that's why my ovens stay ready.
